paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose you are asked to give advice on whether to attend college at home or abroad, write an essay to state your opinion. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您被要求就是否在国内或国外上大学提供建议，请写一篇文章来陈述您的意见。您需要写至少 150 字但不超过 200 字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Let's all stop judging people who talk to themselves. New research says that those who can't seem to keep their
paragraphs.translationZh: 让我们都停止评判那些自言自语的人。新的研究表明，那些似乎无法保留自己的

paragraphs.sourceText: inner monologues ( 独白) in are actually more likely to stay on task, remain __26__ better and show improved perception capabilities. Not bad, really, for some extra muttering.
paragraphs.translationZh: 内心独白实际上更有可能专注于任务，更好地保持专注，并表现出更好的感知能力。确实，对于一些额外的嘀咕来说还不错。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to a series of experiments published in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology by professors Gary Lupyan and Daniel Swignley, the act of using verbal clues to __27__ mental pictures helps people function quicker.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加里·卢皮安（Gary Lupyan）和丹尼尔·斯威格利（Daniel Swignley）教授在《实验心理学季刊》上发表的一系列实验表明，使用言语线索触发心理图像的行为有助于人们更快地发挥作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: In one experiment, they showed pictures of various objects to twenty __28__ and asked them to find just one of those, a banana. Half were __29__ to repeat out loud what they were looking for and the other half kept their lips __30__. Those who talked to themselves found the banana slightly faster than those who didn't, the researchers say. In other experiments, Lupyan and Swignley found that __31__ the name of a common product when on the hunt for it helped quicken someone's pace, but talking about uncommon items showed no advantage and slowed you down.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一项实验中，他们向 20 名志愿者展示了各种物体的图片，并要求他们只找到其中一个，即一根香蕉。一半人被要求大声重复他们正在寻找的东西，而另一半人则保持沉默。研究人员表示，那些自言自语的人发现香蕉的速度比那些不自言自语的人稍快一些。在其他实验中，Lupyan 和 Swignley 发现，在寻找一种常见产品时说出它的名称有助于加快某人的步伐，但谈论不常见的物品并没有任何优势，反而会减慢你的速度。

paragraphs.sourceText: Common research has long held that talking themselves through a task helps children learn, although doing so when you've __32__ matured is not a great sign of __33__. The two professors hope to refute that idea, __34__ that just as when kids walk themselves through a process, adults can benefit from using language not just to communicate, but also to help "augment thinking".
paragraphs.translationZh: 长期以来，常见的研究认为，通过自己的谈话完成一项任务有助于孩子学习，尽管在你明显成熟的时候这样做并不是聪明的标志。两位教授希望反驳这种想法，声称就像孩子们自己经历一个过程一样，成年人可以从使用语言中受益，不仅可以进行交流，还可以帮助“增强思维”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, you are still encouraged to keep the talking at library tones and, whatever you do, keep the information you share simple, like a grocery list. At any __35__, there's still such a thing as too much information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，我们仍然鼓励您以图书馆的语气进行交谈，并且无论您做什么，都要保持分享的信息简单，例如购物清单。无论如何，信息量仍然太多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rich Children and Poor Ones Are Raised Very Differently
paragraphs.translationZh: 富人和穷人的成长方式截然不同

paragraphs.sourceText: according to a new Pew Research Center survey. There are usually two parents, who spend a lot of time reading to children and worrying about their anxiety levels and hectic schedules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据皮尤研究中心的一项新调查。通常有两个父母，他们花大量时间给孩子读书，并担心他们的焦虑程度和繁忙的日程。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. In poor families, meanwhile, children tend to spend their time at home or with extended family. They are more likely to grow up in neighborhoods that their parents say aren't great for raising children, and their parents worry about them getting shot, beaten up or in trouble with the law.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 与此同时，在贫困家庭中，孩子们倾向于在家中或与大家庭一起度过时间。他们更有可能在父母认为不适合抚养孩子的社区长大，他们的父母担心他们遭到枪击、殴打或触犯法律。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. The class differences in child rearing are growing—a symptom of widening inequality with far-reaching consequences. Different upbringings set children on different paths and can deepen socioeconomic divisions, especially because education is strongly linked to earnings. Children grow up learning the skills to succeed in their socioeconomic stratum (阶层), but not necessarily others.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 育儿方面的阶级差异正在扩大——这是不平等现象扩大的征兆，并产生了深远的影响。不同的成长经历会让孩子走上不同的道路，并可能加深社会经济分歧，特别是因为教育与收入密切相关。孩子们在成长过程中学习在自己的社会经济阶层（但不一定是其他阶层）取得成功的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. "Early childhood experiences can be very consequential for children's long-term social, emotional and cognitive development," said Sean Reardon, professor of poverty and inequality in education at Stanford University. "And because those influence educational success and later earnings, early childhood experiences cast a lifelong shadow." The cycle continues: Poorer parents have less time and fewer resources to invest in their children, which can leave children less prepared for school and work, which leads to lower earnings.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 斯坦福大学贫困和教育不平等问题教授肖恩·里尔登 (Sean Reardon) 表示：“童年早期经历对儿童的长期社交、情感和认知发展非常重要。” “由于这些影响教育成功和以后的收入，幼儿时期的经历会留下终生的阴影。”这种循环还在继续：较贫穷的父母投资于孩子的时间和资源较少，这可能导致孩子为上学和工作做好准备不足，从而导致收入下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) American parents want similar things for their children, the Pew report and past research have found: for them to be healthy and happy, honest and ethical, caring and compassionate. There is no best parenting style or philosophy, researchers say, and across income groups, 92% of parents say they are doing a good job at raising their children. Yet they are doing it quite differently. Middle-class and higher-income parents see their children as projects in need of careful cultivation, says Annette Lareau, whose groundbreaking research on the topic was published in her book Unequal Childhoods: Class, Race and Family Life. They try to develop their skills through close supervision and organized activities, and teach children to question authority figures and navigate elite institutions.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 皮尤报告和过去的研究发现，美国父母希望他们的孩子拥有类似的东西：让他们健康快乐、诚实有道德、有爱心和富有同情心。研究人员表示，不存在最好的养育方式或理念，而且在各个收入群体中，92% 的父母表示他们在抚养孩子方面做得很好。然而他们的做法却截然不同。安妮特·拉罗 (Annette Lareau) 表示，中产阶级和高收入父母将他们的孩子视为需要精心培养的项目，她对此主题的开创性研究发表在她的著作《不平等的童年：阶级、种族和家庭生活》中。他们试图通过密切监督和有组织的活动来发展他们的技能，并教孩子们质疑权威人物并驾驭精英机构。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Working-class parents, meanwhile, believe their children will naturally thrive, and give them far greater independence and time for free play. They are taught to be compliant and respectful to adults. There are benefits to both approaches. Working-class children are happier, more independent, complain less and are closer with family members, Ms. Lareau found. Higher-income children are more likely to declare boredom and expect their parents to solve their problems. Yet later on, the more affluent children end up in college and on the way to the middle class, while working-class children tend to struggle. Children from higher-income families are likely to have the skills to navigate bureaucracies and succeed in schools and workplaces, Ms. Lareau said.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 与此同时，工薪阶层的父母相信他们的孩子会自然而然地茁壮成长，并给予他们更大的独立性和自由玩耍的时间。他们被教导要顺从并尊重成年人。两种方法都有好处。拉罗女士发现，工薪阶层的孩子更快乐、更独立、更少抱怨，并且与家人关系更亲密。高收入的孩子更有可能表现出无聊并期望父母解决他们的问题。然而后来，较富裕的孩子最终进入大学并进入中产阶级，而工薪阶层的孩子则往往陷入困境。拉罗女士说，来自高收入家庭的孩子可能具备应对官僚机构并在学校和工作场所取得成功的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. "Do all parents want the most success for their children? Absolutely," she said. "Do some strategies give children more advantages than others in institutions? Probably they do. Will parents be damaging children if they have one fewer organized activity? No, I really doubt it."
paragraphs.translationZh: H. “所有的父母都希望自己的孩子获得最大的成功吗？当然，”她说。 “在机构中，某些策略是否会给孩子们带来比其他孩子更多的优势？可能确实如此。如果父母少参加一项有组织的活动，会不会对孩子造成伤害？不，我真的很怀疑。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Social scientists say the differences arise in part because low-income parents have less money to spend on music class or preschool, and less flexible schedules to take children to museums or attend school events. Extracurricular activities reflect the differences in child rearing in the Pew survey, which was of a nationally representative sample of 1,807 parents. Of families earning more than $75,000 a year, 84% say their children have participated in organized sports over the past year, 64% have done volunteer work and 62% have taken lessons in music, dance or art. Of families earning less than $30,000, 59% of children have done sports, 37% have volunteered and 41% have taken arts classes.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 社会科学家表示，造成这种差异的部分原因是低收入父母花在音乐课或学前班上的钱较少，带孩子去博物馆或参加学校活动的时间安排也不太灵活。皮尤研究中心对全国具有代表性的 1,807 名家长进行了调查，课外活动反映了育儿方面的差异。年收入超过 75,000 美元的家庭中，84% 的家庭表示，他们的孩子在过去一年中参加了有组织的体育活动，64% 的家庭做过志愿者工作，62% 的家庭参加过音乐、舞蹈或艺术课程。在收入低于 30,000 美元的家庭中，59% 的孩子参加过体育运动，37% 的孩子参加过志愿服务，41% 的孩子参加过艺术课程。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Especially in affluent families, children start young. Nearly half of high-earning, college-graduate parents enrolled their children in arts classes before they were 5, compared with one-fifth of low-income, less- educated parents. Nonetheless, 20% of well-off parents say their children's schedules are too hectic, compared with 8% of poorer parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 尤其是在富裕家庭，孩子从小就开始。近一半高收入、大学毕业生的父母在孩子 5 岁之前就让他们参加艺术课程，而低收入、受教育程度较低的父母只有五分之一。尽管如此，20% 的富裕父母表示孩子的日程安排太忙碌，而贫困父母的这一比例为 8%。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Another example is reading aloud, which studies have shown gives children bigger vocabularies and better reading comprehension in school. 71% of parents with a college degree say they do it every day, compared with 33% of those with a high school diploma or less. White parents are more likely than others to read to their children daily, as are married parents. Most affluent parents enroll their children in preschool or day care, while low-income parents are more likely to depend on family members. Discipline techniques vary by education level: 8% of those with a postgraduate degree say they often beat their children, compared with 22% of those with a high school degree or less.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 另一个例子是大声阅读，研究表明，大声阅读可以让孩子在学校拥有更大的词汇量和更好的阅读理解能力。 71% 拥有大学学历的家长表示他们每天都会这样做，而拥有高中或以下学历的家长这一比例为 33%。白人父母比其他人更有可能每天给孩子读书，已婚父母也是如此。大多数富裕的父母让孩子进入学前班或日托中心，而低收入的父母更有可能依赖家庭成员。管教技巧因教育程度而异：拥有研究生学历的人中有 8% 表示他们经常殴打孩子，而高中及以下学历的人中这一比例为 22%。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. The survey also probed attitudes and anxieties. Interestingly, parents' attitudes toward education do not seem to reflect their own educational background as much as a belief in the importance of education for upward mobility. Most American parents say they are not concerned about their children's grades as long as they work hard. But 50% of poor parents say it is extremely important to them that their children earn a college degree, compared with 39% of wealthier parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 该调查还探讨了态度和焦虑。有趣的是，家长对教育的态度似乎并不反映他们自己的教育背景，而是相信教育对于向上流动的重要性。大多数美国家长表示，只要孩子努力学习，他们并不关心孩子的成绩。但 50% 的贫困父母表示，孩子获得大学学位对他们来说极其重要，而富裕父母的这一比例为 39%。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. Less-educated parents, and poorer and black and Latino parents are more likely to believe that there is no such thing as too much involvement in a child's education. Parents who are white, wealthy or college- educated say too much involvement can be bad. Parental anxieties reflect their circumstances. High- earning parents are much more likely to say they live in a good neighborhood for raising children. While bullying is parents' greatest concern over all, nearly half of low-income parents worry their child will get shot, compared with one-fifth of high-income parents. They are more worried about their children being depressed or anxious.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 受教育程度较低的父母，以及较贫穷的黑人和拉丁裔父母更有可能认为，没有过多参与孩子的教育。白人、富有或受过大学教育的父母表示，过多的参与可能是不好的。父母的焦虑反映了他们的情况。高收入父母更有可能说他们生活在一个适合养育孩子的良好社区。虽然欺凌是父母最关心的问题，但近一半的低收入父母担心他们的孩子会被枪杀，而高收入父母只有五分之一担心。他们更担心孩子抑郁或焦虑。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. In the Pew survey, middle-class families earning between $30,000 and $75,000 a year fell right between working-class and high-earning parents on issues like the quality of their neighborhood for raising children, participation in extracurricular activities and involvement in their children' s education.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 在皮尤研究中心的调查中, 年收入在 30,000 美元到 75,000 美元之间的中产阶级家庭在抚养孩子的社区质量、参加课外活动和参与孩子教育等问题上正好处于工人阶级和高收入家庭之间。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Children were not always raised so differently. The achievement gap between children from high- and low-income families is 30-40% larger among children born in 2001 than those born 25 years earlier, according to Mr. Reardon's research. People used to live near people of different income levels; neighborhoods are now more segregated by income. More than a quarter of children live in single-parent households—a historic high, according to Pew—and these children are three times as likely to live in poverty as those who live with married parents. Meanwhile, growing income inequality has coincided with the increasing importance of a college degree for earning a middle-class wage. P) Yet there are recent signs that the gap could be starting to shrink. In the past decade, even as income inequality has grown, some of the socioeconomic differences in parenting, like reading to children and going to libraries, have narrowed. Q) Public policies aimed at young children have helped, including public preschool programs and reading initiatives. Addressing differences in the earliest years, it seems, could reduce inequality in the next generation.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 孩子们的成长方式并不总是如此不同。里尔登先生的研究表明，2001 年出生的孩子与 25 年前出生的孩子相比，高收入和低收入家庭的孩子之间的成绩差距要大 30-40%。人们曾经住在不同收入水平的人附近；现在，社区之间的收入隔离更加严重。皮尤研究中心的数据显示，超过四分之一的儿童生活在单亲家庭中，这是历史最高水平，而这些儿童生活在贫困中的可能性是与已婚父母一起生活的儿童的三倍。与此同时，收入不平等的加剧与大学学位对于赚取中产阶级工资的重要性日益增加同时发生。 P) 然而，最近有迹象表明差距可能开始缩小。在过去的十年中，尽管收入不平等加剧，但养育子女方面的一些社会经济差异（例如给孩子读书和去图书馆）已经缩小。问）针对幼儿的公共政策有所帮助，包括公共学前教育计划和阅读倡议。解决最早几年的差异似乎可以减少下一代的不平等。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Working-class parents teach their children to be obedient and show respect to adults.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.工人阶级的父母教导孩子要服从并尊重成人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. American parents, whether rich or poor, have similar expectations of their children despite different ways of parenting.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 美国父母，无论富有还是贫穷，尽管养育方式不同，但对孩子有着相似的期望。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. While rich parents are more concerned with their children's psychological well-being, poor parents are more worried about their children's safety.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 富有的父母更关心孩子的心理健康，而贫穷的父母更担心孩子的安全。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The increasing differences in child rearing between rich and poor families reflect growing social inequality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 富裕家庭和贫困家庭在抚养子女方面的差异日益扩大，反映出社会不平等日益加剧。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Parenting approaches of working-class and affluent families both have advantages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 工人阶级和富裕家庭的养育方式各有优点。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Higher-income families and working-class families now tend to live in different neighborhoods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 高收入家庭和工人阶级家庭现在往往居住在不同的社区。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Physical punishment is used much less by well-educated parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 受过良好教育的父母很少使用体罚。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Ms. Lareau doesn't believe participating in fewer after-class activities will negatively affect children's development.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. Lareau女士认为参加较少的课外活动不会对儿童的发展产生负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Wealthy parents are concerned about their children's mental health and busy schedules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 富裕的父母关心孩子的心理健康和繁忙的日程。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some socioeconomic differences in child rearing have shrunk in the past ten years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 过去十年来，儿童抚养方面的一些社会经济差异已经缩小。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Tennessee's technical and community colleges will not outsource (外包) management of their facilities to a private company, a decision one leader said was bolstered by an analysis of spending at each campus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 田纳西州的技术和社区学院不会将其设施的管理外包给私营公司，一位领导人表示，对每个校园支出的分析支持了这一决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: In an email sent Monday to college presidents in the Tennessee Board of Regents system, outgoing Chancellor John Morgan said an internal analysis showed that each campus' spending on facilities management fell well below the industry standards identified by the state. Morgan said those findings—which included data from the system's 13 community colleges, 27 technical colleges and six universities—were part of the decision not to move forward with Governor Bill Haslam's proposal to privatize management of state buildings in an effort to save money.
paragraphs.translationZh: 即将卸任的校长约翰·摩根在周一发给田纳西州董事会系统大学校长的一封电子邮件中表示，一项内部分析显示，每个校园在设施管理上的支出远远低于该州确定的行业标准。摩根表示，这些调查结果包括来自该系统 13 所社区学院、27 所技术学院和 6 所大学的数据，是决定不推进州长比尔·哈斯拉姆 (Bill Haslam) 为省钱而将州立建筑管理私有化的提议的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: "While these numbers are still being validated by the state, we feel any adjustments they might suggest will be immaterial," Morgan wrote to the presidents. "System institutions are operating very efficiently based on this analysis, raising the question of the value of pursuing a broad scale outsourcing initiative."
paragraphs.translationZh: 摩根在给总统们的信中写道：“虽然这些数字仍在得到国家的验证，但我们认为他们可能建议的任何调整都是无关紧要的。” “根据这一分析，系统机构的运作非常高效，这提出了推行大规模外包计划的价值问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Worker's advocates have criticized Haslam's plan, saying it would mean some campus workers would lose their jobs or benefits. Haslam has said colleges would be free to opt in or out of the out souring plan, which has not been finalized.
paragraphs.translationZh: 工人倡导者批评哈斯拉姆的计划，称这将意味着一些校园工人将失去工作或福利。哈斯拉姆表示，大学可以自由选择加入或退出外包计划，但该计划尚未最终确定。

paragraphs.sourceText: Morgan notified the Haslam administration of his decision to opt out in a letter sent last week. That letter, which includes several concerns Morgan has with the plan, was originally obtained by The Commercial Appeal in Memphis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摩根在上周发出的一封信中通知了哈斯拉姆政府他选择退出的决定。这封信最初是由孟菲斯的《商业上诉报》获得的，其中包括摩根对该计划的一些担忧。

paragraphs.sourceText: In an email statement from the state's Office of Customer Focused Government, which is examining the possibility of outsourcing, spokeswoman Michelle R. Martin said officials were still working to analyze the data from the Board of Regents. Data on management expenses at the college system and in other state departments will be part of a "business justification" the state will use as officials deliberate the specifics of an outsourcing plan.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该州以客户为中心的政府办公室正在研究外包的可能性，发言人米歇尔·R·马丁(Michelle R. Martin)在一份电子邮件声明中表示，官员们仍在分析来自董事会的数据。大学系统和其他州政府部门的管理费用数据将成为州政府在官员审议外包计划细节时使用的“商业理由”的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: "The state's facilities management project team is still in the process of developing its business justification and expects to have that completed and available to the public at the end of February," Martin said. "At this time there is nothing to take action on since the analysis has yet to be completed."
paragraphs.translationZh: 马丁说：“该州的设施管理项目团队仍在制定其商业理由，预计将于二月底完成并向公众提供。” “目前没有什么可采取行动的，因为分析尚未完成。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Morgan's comments on outsourcing mark the second time this month that he has come out against one of Haslam's plans for higher education in Tennessee. Morgan said last week that he would retire at the end of January because of the governor's proposal to split off six universities of the Board of Regents system and create separate governing boards for each of them. In his resignation letter, Morgan called the reorganization "unworkable".
paragraphs.translationZh: 摩根对外包的评论标志着他本月第二次公开反对哈斯拉姆在田纳西州的一项高等教育计划。摩根上周表示，他将于一月底退休，因为州长提议将董事会系统中的六所大学分开，并为每所大学设立独立的理事会。摩根在辞职信中称重组“行不通”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Beginning in the late sixteenth century, it became fashionable for young aristocrats to visit Paris, Venice,
paragraphs.translationZh: 从十六世纪末开始，年轻贵族游览巴黎、威尼斯、

paragraphs.sourceText: Florence, and above all, Rome, as the culmination (终极) of their classical education. Thus was born the idea of the Grand Tour, a practice which introduced Englishmen, Germans, Scandinavians, and also Americans to the art and culture of France and Italy for the next 300 years. Travel was arduous and costly throughout the period, possible only for a privileged class—the same that produced gentlemen scientists, authors, antique experts, and patrons of the arts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 佛罗伦萨，尤其是罗马，是他们古典教育的顶峰（终极）。由此诞生了“壮游”的想法，在接下来的 300 年里，这一实践将英国人、德国人、斯堪的纳维亚人和美国人介绍给法国和意大利的艺术和文化。整个时期的旅行既艰苦又昂贵，只有特权阶层才有可能——这个阶层产生了绅士科学家、作家、古董专家和艺术赞助人。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Grand Tourist was typically a young man with a thorough grounding in Greek and Latin literature as well as some leisure time, some means, and some interest in art. The German traveler Johann Winckelmann pioneered the field of art history with his comprehensive study of Greek and Roman sculpture; he was portrayed by his friend Anton Raphael Mengs at the beginning of his long residence in Rome. Most Grand Tourists, however, stayed for briefer periods and set out with less scholarly intentions, accompanied by a teacher or guardian, and expected to return home with souvenirs of their travels as well as an understanding of art and architecture formed by exposure to great masterpieces.
paragraphs.translationZh: 伟大的旅游者通常是一位年轻人，对希腊和拉丁文学有深入的了解，并且有一些闲暇时间、一些手段和对艺术的一些兴趣。德国旅行家约翰·温克尔曼（Johann Winckelmann）凭借对希腊和罗马雕塑的全面研究开创了艺术史领域；他在罗马长期居住之初由他的朋友安东·拉斐尔·门斯饰演。然而，大多数大游客在老师或监护人的陪同下停留时间较短，出发时没有多少学术意图，并期望带着旅行纪念品以及通过接触伟大杰作而形成的对艺术和建筑的理解回家。

paragraphs.sourceText: London was a frequent starting point for Grand Tourists, and Paris a compulsory destination; many traveled to the Netherlands, some to Switzerland and Germany, and a very few adventurers to Spain, Greece, or Turkey. The essential place to visit, however, was Italy. The British traveler Charles Thompson spoke for many Grand Tourists when in 1744 he described himself as "being impatiently desirous of viewing a country so famous in history, a country which once gave laws to the world, and which is at present the greatest school of music and painting, contains the noblest productions of sculpture and architecture, and is filled with cabinets of rarities, and collections of all kinds of historical relics". Within Italy, the great focus was Rome, whose ancient ruins and more recent achievements were shown to every Grand Tourist. Panini's Ancient Rome and Modem Rome represent the sights most prized, including celebrated Greco-Roman statues and views of famous ruins, fountains, and churches. Since there were few museums anywhere in Europe before the close of the eighteenth century, Grand Tourists often saw paintings and sculptures by gaining admission to private collections, and many were eager to acquire examples of Greco-Roman and Italian art for their own collections. In England, where architecture was increasingly seen as an aristocratic pursuit, noblemen often applied what they learned from the villas of Palladio in the Veneto and the
paragraphs.translationZh: 伦敦是大旅游者经常选择的出发地，而巴黎则是必去的目的地；许多人去了荷兰，一些人去了瑞士和德国，还有极少数冒险家去了西班牙、希腊或土耳其。然而，最重要的游览地点是意大利。英国旅行家查尔斯·汤普森（Charles Thompson）在 1744 年描述自己“迫不及待地想参观一个历史上如此著名的国家，一个曾经为世界制定法律的国家，目前是最伟大的音乐和绘画学校，拥有最高贵的雕塑和建筑作品，并充满了珍品柜子和各种历史文物收藏”，这代表了许多伟大的游客”。在意大利，最大的焦点是罗马，它的古代遗迹和最近的成就向每一位伟大的游客展示。帕尼尼的古罗马和现代罗马代表了最珍贵的景点，包括著名的希腊罗马雕像以及著名遗址、喷泉和教堂的景观。由于十八世纪末之前欧洲各地几乎没有博物馆，大游客经常通过获得私人收藏的门票来参观绘画和雕塑，许多人渴望获得希腊罗马和意大利艺术的例子作为自己的收藏。在英国，建筑越来越被视为贵族的追求，贵族们经常运用他们从威尼托的帕拉迪奥别墅和意大利的别墅中学到的东西。
